message.content: Prices across the semiconductor industry are moving up rather than down [D1]. Mature-node chip shortages are expected to persist for several years and have turned supply chain management into a pricing lever [D1]. Intel CPU prices are reportedly rising again as Qualcomm and MediaTek target the gaps left in IPC and IoT [D1]. Tungsten prices have surged as US and China restrictions tighten supply for chips, aerospace and defense [D1]. The strongest driver is AI demand, which is stretching the global chip industry beyond its usual planning cycle, with fast-changing procurement needs, labor shortages and infrastructure constraints affecting markets far beyond Taiwan [D5]. That demand is visible in the sales data, with global semiconductor sales running above their level of the same month a year earlier [D4], and the industry is expected to grow strongly [D2]. Japan's semiconductor market is likewise forecast to increase [D6]. Weighing against further price gains is the expanding supply base in China, where chip output has multiplied over the past decade as manufacturing capacity grew across mature-node chips, memory and packaging [D3].
